construction_markdown:
No leaderboard code is claimed. The audited conditional architecture uses a binary linear inner code `[2^a,m,d]_2` and an ordinary `N=2^(30-a)`-point Reed–Solomon code `[N,K,N-K+1]` over `F_(2^m)`, where `N≤2^m`. Binary concatenation would have length `2^30`, dimension `mK`, and certified distance at least `d(N-K+1)`.

After exact finite elimination for `m≤18`, every product-distance-certified route with dimension above 1040 requires inner length 16384. The best unresolved conditional instances are:

| Inner code required | Outer parameters | Conditional binary result |
|---|---|---|
| `[16384,16,8190]_2` | `[65536,113,65424]_(2^16)` | `[2^30,1808,≥535822560]_2` |
| `[16384,17,8188]_2` | `[65536,97,65440]_(2^17)` | `[2^30,1649,≥535822720]_2` |
| `[16384,18,8184]_2` | `[65536,65,65472]_(2^18)` | `[2^30,1170,≥535822848]_2` |

Existence of all three displayed inner codes is unresolved, so these are gateways rather than constructions.

distance_audit: The Reed–Solomon product `d(N-K+1)` is used only as a sufficient distance certificate; no claim is made that it equals the concatenated code's true distance.
Every cubic LP polynomial is nonpositive at every permitted nonzero distance on the binary parity lattice and has nonnegative Krawtchouk coefficients.
Each residual argument chooses an actual minimum-weight word. Short residuals are padded only with zero coordinates, preserving cardinality and minimum distance.
For the three conditional endpoint rows, the exact certified products are `D+224`, `D+384`, and `D+512`.
For the fixed affine encoder, the exact block-weight identity is `wt(H^A(u))=2^14(32768-N_0(u)+N_1(u))`; hence the target is equivalent to `N_0-N_1≤64` for every nonzero outer word.
explicitness_audit: All integer choices, ceilings, Griesmer sums, residual lengths, cubic coefficients, and payoff products are stated explicitly.
No random existence, sampling, numerical optimization, or hidden asymptotic constant is used.
The remaining inner codes are explicitly labeled unresolved and are not counted as constructions.
The unequal-block result is scoped to an `F_65536`-linear outer code of length 32768 with coordinatewise binary-linear maps.
The additive-maximality result is scoped to superspaces of the degree-64 evaluation code under the fixed affine inner encoder.

The workspace was read-only, so no proof, record, or message-board file was mutated; the complete posts are returned in `discussion_posts`. Consequently the validator and dashboard build were not invoked as a publication step.

obstructions: Within the ordinary equal-block RS design space using the standard product-distance proof and `m≤18`, certified dimension is at most 1808.
No binary code, even nonlinear, of length 8192, cardinality at least `2^17`, and distance at least 4090 exists.
No binary linear `[32768,17,≥16383]` or `[32768,18,≥16381]` code exists.
Any surviving `[16384,18,≥8184]` code has exact distance 8184; dimensions 17 and 16 have ceilings 8188 and 8190 respectively.
No strict extension of `RM(1,14)` can serve as one of the remaining inner codes: Parseval forces a word of weight at most 8128.

For the fixed `F_65536`, length-32768 outer architecture, arbitrary unequal binary block lengths, interleaving, and zero padding still force outer dimension `K≤65`, hence binary dimension at most 1040.
The shared reciprocal-sum witness proves that the existing degree-64 RS–affine code has no strict additive outer supercode under its fixed affine inner encoder.
The 1808 cap does not cover `m≥19`, non-RS outer codes, weighted-shell arguments stronger than the ordinary product bound, or unrelated binary constructions.

parameter_ledger.derivation: To improve dimension 1040, use `K_0=floor(1040/m)+1` and require `d≥ceil(D/(N-K_0+1))`.
Exact Griesmer-relaxed maximization over all admissible powers of two.
Residual plus cubics at lengths 16385 and 16387.
Scalar-orbit averaging with `Q=65536`, `L=32768`, and total binary length at most `2^30`.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem and scope

Let `D=535822336`. Consider equal-block concatenations formed from a binary linear inner code `[2^a,m,d]_2` and an ordinary `N=2^(30-a)`-point Reed–Solomon outer code over `F_(2^m)`, with `N≤2^m`. When distance is certified by the ordinary product bound, every such construction with `m≤18` and distance at least `D` has binary dimension at most 1808. If its dimension exceeds 1040, then `a=14` and its inner parameters belong to exactly one of

`[16384,16,d]`, `8185≤d≤8190`;

`[16384,17,d]`, `8184≤d≤8188`;

`[16384,18,8184]`.

This is an obstruction theorem, not an existence assertion.

## 1. Concatenation and finite Griesmer ledger

The concatenation has length `2^a N=2^30`, binary dimension `mK`, and product-distance certificate

`d(C)≥d(N-K+1)`.

Write

`g_m(d)=sum_(i=0)^(m-1) ceil(d/2^i)`.

The binary Griesmer bound requires `g_m(d)≤2^a`. To obtain `mK>1040`, necessarily

`K≥K_0=floor(1040/m)+1`

and therefore

`d≥delta(a,m)=ceil(D/(N-K_0+1))`.

Exact evaluation of these finite integer expressions leaves only seven pairs:

| `m` | `a` | `2^a` | `N` | `K_0` | `delta` | `g_m(delta)` | Griesmer maximum `d_G` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|16|14|16384|65536|66|8185|16374|8191|
|17|13|8192|131072|62|4090|8185|4094|
|17|14|16384|65536|62|8184|16371|8190|
|17|15|32768|32768|62|16383|32768|16383|
|18|13|8192|131072|58|4090|8186|4093|
|18|14|16384|65536|58|8184|16372|8190|
|18|15|32768|32768|58|16381|32766|16382|

Every other admissible `(m,a)` with `m≤18` has `delta>d_G`. As a cross-check, the relaxed Griesmer maxima for `m=1,...,15` are respectively `2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18,30,55,108,221,462,975`, all below 1040.

## 2. Parity-lattice cubic LP lemma

For binary length `n`, put `y=n-2x`, `t=n-2d`, and choose `r` with `r≡n (mod 2)`. Define

`F(x)=(y-t)(y+r)(y+r+2)`.

For every allowed integer distance `x≥d`, one has `y≤t`. The only interval where `(y+r)(y+r+2)<0` is `(-r-2,-r)`, which contains no integer of parity `n`. Hence `F(x)≤0` on every allowed nonzero distance.

Using `K_1=y`, `K_2=(y^2-n)/2`, and `K_3=(y^3-(3n-2)y)/6`, the expansion is

`F=f_0 K_0+f_1 K_1+f_2 K_2+6K_3`,

where

`f_0=n(2r+2-t)-tr(r+2)`,

`f_1=r(r+2)-2t(r+1)+3n-2`,

`f_2=4r+4-2t`.

All coefficients used below are nonnegative and `f_0>0`. For any binary code `C`, Krawtchouk positivity gives `sum_(u,v∈C) K_i(dist(u,v))≥0`. Consequently

`f_0|C|^2≤sum_(u,v)F(dist(u,v))≤|C|F(0)`,

so `|C|≤F(0)/f_0`.

At `(n,d,r)=(8192,4090,630)`, the coefficients are

`(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)=(5462080,407590,2500,6)`,

and `F(0)=636774783040`. Thus

`A_2(8192,4090)≤floor(F(0)/f_0)=116581<2^17`.

This eliminates both length-8192 rows, even without linearity.

## 3. Residual closures

If `C` is binary linear and `c` is an actual minimum word of weight `w`, restriction of `C/<c>` to the complement of `supp(c)` gives a linear residual code `[n-w,k-1,d'≥ceil(w/2)]`. Indeed, for any lift `z`, the sum of the weights of `z` and `z+c` is `w+2 wt(z|_(complement))`; both are at least `w`.

A hypothetical `[32768,17,≥16383]` code has actual minimum 16383 by Griesmer and residualizes to `[16385,16,≥8192]`. The cubic with `r=8191` gives `A_2(16385,8192)≤49156<2^16`.

A hypothetical `[32768,18,≥16381]` residualizes, after harmless zero padding, to `[16387,17,≥8191]`. The cubic with `r=2731` gives

`A_2(16387,8191)≤114854<2^17`.

Thus both length-32768 rows are impossible.

At length 16384, the same argument gives:

- `[16384,16,≥8191]` residualizes to `[8193,15,≥4096]`; the `r=4095` cubic gives exactly `24580<2^15`.
- `[16384,17,≥8189]` residualizes after padding to `[8195,16,≥4095]`; the `r=1365` cubic gives `57510<2^16`.
- `[16384,18,≥8185]` residualizes after padding to `[8199,17,≥4093]`; the `r=585` cubic gives `125387<2^17`.

Therefore the three surviving distance ranges are precisely the ranges stated in the theorem.

The eliminated length-8192 rows can certify at most dimensions 561 and 594; the eliminated length-32768 rows can certify at most 1037 and 1026. For the remaining length-16384 rows, `K=65537-ceil(D/d)`, so the largest possible product-bound dimensions are 1808, 1649, and 1170. Hence the whole audited class is capped at 1808.

## 4. Forced structure of the dimension-18 endpoint

Suppose a binary `[16384,18,8184]` code exists. Residualizing a minimum word gives `[8200,17,≥4092]`. Its distance must be exactly 4092: otherwise residualization and padding would give `[4107,16,≥2047]`, while the cubic `(n,d,r)=(4107,2047,293)` has coefficients `(1237870,91110,1150,6)` and bounds its size by `64058<2^16`.

Lift a weight-4092 residual word. The original word, its lift, and their sum must all have weight 8184. Their four coordinate-pattern multiplicities are therefore

`m_00=4108`, `m_01=m_10=m_11=4092`.

Residualizing twice leaves `[4108,16,d_2]` with `d_2≥2046`. If `d_2≥2048`, another residual would produce, after padding, `[2060,15,≥1024]`; the cubic `(2060,1024,158)` bounds its size by `30838<2^15`. Hence `d_2∈{2046,2047}`.

If `d_2=2046`, averaging the eight coset shifts shows that every nonzero word in the resulting 3-dimensional subcode has weight exactly 8184. Fourier inversion on its seven nonzero column patterns gives multiplicity 2046 for each, leaving 2062 zero-pattern coordinates and a residual `[2062,15,≥1023]`. If `d_2=2047`, ordinary residualization leaves `[2061,15,≥1024]`.

## 5. Two further alphabet-reduction obstructions

First, no surviving inner code can strictly contain `RM(1,14)`. If `f` lies outside this Reed–Muller subcode, Parseval gives

`sum_a |W_f(a)|^2=2^28`,

so some Walsh coefficient has magnitude at least 128. Choosing the affine constant with the favorable sign produces a nonzero word of weight at most `(16384-128)/2=8128`, below every surviving threshold.

Second, let `W≤F_Q^L` be `F_Q`-linear of dimension `K`, and let coordinate maps `phi_j:F_Q→F_2^(ell_j)` be binary-linear, with total output length `M`. Sort the `ell_j` decreasingly. A nonzero word of `W` can be chosen to vanish in the first `K-1` coordinates, so its active binary length is at most `M(L-K+1)/L`. Averaging its `Q-1` nonzero scalar multiples gives

`d≤[Q/(2(Q-1))][(L-K+1)/L]M`.

For `Q=65536`, `L=32768`, and `M≤2^30`, `K=66` would put this upper bound below `D`, since

`32704·65535-32703·65536=32832>0`.

Thus `K≤65` and binary dimension is at most `16K=1040`, even with unequal block lengths, arbitrary coordinate interleaving, and zero padding.

Finally, the independently verified reciprocal-sum lemma closes additive augmentation of the fixed degree-64 RS–affine construction. In `F=F_2[theta]/(theta^16+theta^5+theta^3+theta^2+1)`, let `A=span{1,theta,...,theta^14}` and `D_0` be evaluation on `A` of polynomials of degree at most 64. Under the affine encoder, target distance is equivalent to `N_0-N_1≤64`.

If a strict binary-linear superspace `D` of `D_0` preserved this inequality, interpolation on every 64-set `R⊂A` would force

`sum_(x∈A\R) 1/G_R(x)=0`, where `G_R(X)=product_(r∈R)(X-r)`.

Take `U=span{1,...,theta^5}`, `b=theta^6`, and `R=(U\{0})∪{b}`. The explicit subspace-polynomial calculation in the shared verified record gives

`sum_(x∈A\R)1/G_R(x)=0x0990≠0`,

a contradiction. Hence the fixed affine-inner code has no strict additive outer extension preserving the target distance.

proof_steps.proof: Concatenation has one binary block per outer symbol. An outer word has at least `N-K+1` nonzero symbols, each encoded to an inner word of weight at least `d`; injectivity gives binary dimension `mK`.
Evaluate `K_0=floor(1040/m)+1`, `delta=ceil(D/(N-K_0+1))`, and `g_m(delta)` over the finite domain `m≤18`, `N=2^(30-a)≤2^m`. Exactly the seven rows displayed in the proof survive.
proof_steps.statement: Only seven `(m,a)` pairs can exceed dimension 1040 under the product certificate.

proof_steps.proof: The adjacent roots `-r-2,-r` contain no allowed value of `y=n-2x`. Nonnegative Krawtchouk coefficients and character-sum positivity give `|C|≤F(0)/f_0`.
proof_steps.statement: The stated parity-lattice cubic is a valid Delsarte cardinality certificate.

proof_steps.proof: The exact cubic evaluations exclude distance 4090 at length 8192, the required length-32768 codes, and distances 8191, 8189, and 8185 at length 16384 for dimensions 16, 17, and 18 respectively.
proof_steps.statement: Only the three stated length-16384 distance ranges remain.

proof_steps.proof: For each hypothetical inner code set `K=65537-ceil(D/d)`. The endpoint arithmetic gives `(m,d,K,mK)=(16,8190,113,1808)`, `(17,8188,97,1649)`, and `(18,8184,65,1170)`.
proof_steps.statement: If the three endpoint inner codes exist, they yield the stated concatenations.

proof_steps.proof: Successive residual minima are forced to 4092 and then 2046 or 2047 by the exact cubics at `(4107,2047)` and `(2060,1024)`. Weight averaging determines the coordinate-pattern multiplicities.
proof_steps.statement: Every hypothetical `[16384,18,8184]` code has the forced residual and constant-weight structure stated above.

proof_steps.proof: A Boolean function outside `RM(1,14)` has a Walsh coefficient of magnitude at least 128; choosing its sign yields a word of weight at most 8128.
proof_steps.statement: No surviving inner code can strictly contain `RM(1,14)`.

proof_steps.proof: Kill the `K-1` largest coordinates, then average all nonzero field multiples. Each nonzero binary functional is one on exactly `Q/2` nonzero scalars, yielding the stated upper bound.
proof_steps.statement: For `Q=65536`, `L=32768`, arbitrary coordinatewise binary maps of total length at most `2^30` force `K≤65`.

proof_steps.proof: Interpolation would force a reciprocal sum to vanish for every 64-set, while the explicit set `(U\{0})∪{theta^6}` gives the nonzero value `0x0990`.
proof_steps.statement: The fixed degree-64 RS–affine construction has no strict additive outer supercode preserving the target distance.

theorem_statement: For ordinary equal-block Reed–Solomon concatenation using the standard product-distance certificate, every exact-length `2^30` construction with binary inner dimension `m≤18` and distance at least 535822336 has dimension at most 1808. Any such design exceeding dimension 1040 must use a length-16384 inner code in exactly one of three ranges: `[16384,16,8185..8190]`, `[16384,17,8184..8188]`, or `[16384,18,8184]`. No code realizing these gateways is presently proved.
title: Complete m≤18 RS alphabet-reduction ledger and length-16384 endpoint obstructions
